summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, type 2 diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and diabetic neuropathy was admitted after developing hypotension and dyspnea during dialysis. He later reported chest pressure, palpitations, and nausea, prompting evaluation for acute coronary syndrome. Workup including serial troponins and EKG showed no evidence of myocardial infarction. His symptoms resolved with supportive care, and he remained hemodynamically stable. A left leg ultrasound ruled out DVT, and chest imaging showed stable mild pulmonary edema. He was monitored overnight, required no dialysis during admission, and was discharged back to an extended care facility with no medication changes and instructions to monitor weight and symptoms.
